3/4 But something shifts around minute three. The urgency flattens. The inner noise becomes background again, like it's supposed to be. You stop white-knuckling through the silence and start actually noticing it. There's space between thoughts. Not enlightenment space. Just room to breathe differently.

4/4 Four minutes won't rewire your nervous system. But it cracks the pattern enough that you start seeing how much of your day you're running on reaction fuel. The real work isn't sitting in silence. captions.threads:
so the AI Mastermind thing keeps coming up in conversations. people ask if it's worth the in-person experience and honestly, it depends on where you're at. if you're a creator who's already playing with AI tools but feel like you're missing something in how it all connects, or you're neurodivergent and need actual humans in the room to think better, this hits different than another online course.

the real question is whether you need permission and structure to go deeper. some people do their best work alone with a tutorial. other people need the specific friction of being in a room with other weird ambitious folks who get it. if that second thing sounds like you, the in-person part matters.

i'm not going to pretend it's for everyone. if you're building something and you're already moving fast, you might not need it. but if you feel stuck between knowing enough to be dangerous and knowing enough to be good, the mastermind format actually works because you're working through problems with people who speak your language.
